units.title: Smooth positive approximation of a measurable time coefficient
units.statement: For every measurable coefficient with the stated almost-everywhere range on \([a,b]\), there is a globally smooth real function \(g\) that is strictly positive and at most \(C+\varepsilon\) at every point of that interval, and whose integrated absolute error is less than \(\varepsilon\).
units.formula: \exists g\in C^\infty(\mathbb R),\quad 0<g(t)\le C+\varepsilon\ (a\le t\le b),\qquad \int_a^b |g(t)-f(t)|\,dt<\varepsilon.

steps.title: Approximate by a bounded continuous function
steps.text: The finite interval and the bound on \(f\) give integrability. Apply continuous approximation with half the error budget.
steps.lean:
let ν := volume.restrict (Icc a b)
  have hν : ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, t ∈ Icc a b := ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Icc
  have hfI : Integrable f ν :=
    Integrable.of_bound hf.aestronglyMeasurable C
      (hRange.mono fun t ht => by simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ht.1] using ht.2)
  obtain ⟨q, hq, hqI⟩ := hfI.exists_boundedContinuous_integral_sub_le (half_pos hε)

steps.title: Clip the continuous approximation to the allowed range
steps.text: Set \(u(t)=\max(0,\min(C,q(t)))\). This is continuous and takes values in \([0,C]\) everywhere. Projection onto this interval cannot increase the distance to an almost-everywhere value of \(f\).
steps.lean:
let u (t : ℝ) := max 0 (min C (q t))
  have huC : Continuous u := continuous_const.max (continuous_const.min q.continuous)
  have huRange (t : ℝ) : u t ∈ Icc 0 C := ⟨le_max_left _ _, max_le hC (min_le_left _ _)⟩
  have huI : Integrable u ν :=
    Integrable.of_bound huC.aestronglyMeasurable C (ae_of_all _ fun t => by
      simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (huRange t).1] using (huRange t).2)
  have hClip : ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, ‖u t - f t‖ ≤ ‖f t - q t‖ := hRange.mono fun t ht => by
    change 0 ≤ f t ∧ f t ≤ C at ht
    simp only [u, Real.norm_eq_abs]
    rcases le_or_gt (q t) 0 with hq0 | hq0
    · rw [max_eq_left ((min_le_right C (q t)).trans hq0)]
      rw [abs_of_nonpos (by linarith [ht.1]), abs_of_nonneg (by linarith [ht.1])]
      linarith
    rcases le_or_gt C (q t) with hqC | hqC
    · rw [min_eq_left hqC, max_eq_right hC]
      rw [abs_of_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr ht.2), abs_of_nonpos (by linarith [ht.2])]
      linarith
    rw [min_eq_right hqC.le, max_eq_right hq0.le, abs_sub_comm]
  have hApprox : (∫ t, ‖u t - f t‖ ∂ν) ≤ ε / 2 :=
    (integral_mono_ae (huI.sub hfI).norm (hfI.sub hqI).norm hClip).trans hq

steps.title: Smooth on a compact neighborhood
steps.text: Write \(L=b-a\) and choose \(\delta=\varepsilon/[4(L+1)]\). Uniform continuity on the compact closed one-neighborhood of the interval lets the smooth approximation theorem produce a globally smooth \(v\) with the required error on the interval.
steps.lean:
let δ := ε / (4 * (b - a + 1))
  have hLen := sub_nonneg.mpr hab
  have hDen : 0 < 4 * (b - a + 1) := by positivity
  have hδ : 0 < δ := div_pos hε hDen
  have hδEq : δ * (4 * (b - a + 1)) = ε := div_mul_cancel₀ _ hDen.ne'
  have hδE : 2 * δ ≤ ε := by nlinarith [mul_nonneg hδ.le hLen]
  have hδL : 2 * δ * (b - a) < ε / 2 := by nlinarith
  have hK : IsCompact (Metric.cthickening 1 (Icc a b)) := isCompact_Icc.cthickening
  obtain ⟨η, hη, hUniform⟩ := Metric.uniformContinuousOn_iff.mp
    (hK.uniformContinuousOn_of_continuous huC.continuousOn) (δ / 2) (half_pos hδ)
  obtain ⟨v, hv, hvNear⟩ :=
    huC.exists_contDiff_dist_le_of_forall_mem_ball_dist_le (lt_min one_pos hη)
  have hvClose (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc a b) : dist (v t) (u t) ≤ δ / 2 := by
    apply hvNear t
    intro z hz
    rw [Metric.mem_ball, lt_min_iff] at hz
    exact (hUniform z (mem_cthickening_of_dist_le _ t _ _ ht hz.1.le) t
      (self_subset_cthickening _ ht) hz.2).le

steps.title: Shift to obtain strict positivity
steps.text: Set \(g=v+\delta\). Since \(0\le u\le C\), the shift gives strict positivity. The estimate \(2\delta\le\varepsilon\) also gives the claimed upper bound. Boundedness on the finite interval yields all integral expressions used below.
steps.lean:
let w (t : ℝ) := v t + δ
  have hw : ContDiff ℝ ∞ w := hv.add contDiff_const
  have hwRange (t : ℝ) (ht : t ∈ Icc a b) : 0 < w t ∧ w t ≤ C + ε := by
    have h := abs_le.mp (by simpa [Real.dist_eq] using hvClose t ht)
    exact ⟨by dsimp [w]; linarith [h.1, (huRange t).1],
      by dsimp [w]; linarith [h.2, (huRange t).2]⟩
  have hwI : Integrable w ν :=
    Integrable.of_bound hw.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable (C + ε) (hν.mono fun t ht => by
      simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (hwRange t ht).1.le] using (hwRange t ht).2)

steps.title: Add the two error budgets
steps.text: The smoothing and shift cost at most \(2\delta L<\varepsilon/2\) in integral. The triangle inequality combines this with the clipped approximation.
steps.lean:
have hwClose : ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, ‖‖w t - u t‖‖ ≤ 2 * δ := hν.mono fun t ht => by
    have h := abs_le.mp (by simpa [Real.dist_eq] using hvClose t ht)
    rw [Real.norm_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg _), Real.norm_eq_abs]
    exact abs_le.mpr ⟨by dsimp [w]; linarith [h.1], by dsimp [w]; linarith [h.2]⟩
  have hνReal : ν.real univ = b - a := by
    rw [Measure.real_def, Measure.restrict_apply_univ, Real.volume_Icc, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hLen]
  have hwU : (∫ t, ‖w t - u t‖ ∂ν) ≤ 2 * δ * (b - a) := by
    calc
      _ ≤ ‖∫ t, ‖w t - u t‖ ∂ν‖ := le_abs_self _
      _ ≤ 2 * δ * (b - a) := hνReal ▸ norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const hwClose
  refine ⟨w, hw, hwRange, ?_⟩
  change (∫ t, ‖w t - f t‖ ∂ν) < ε
  calc
    _ ≤ ∫ t, ‖w t - u t‖ + ‖u t - f t‖ ∂ν := integral_mono_ae (hwI.sub hfI).norm
      ((hwI.sub huI).norm.add (huI.sub hfI).norm)
      (ae_of_all _ fun t => by simpa [Real.dist_eq, Real.norm_eq_abs] using dist_triangle (w t) (u t) (f t))
    _ = (∫ t, ‖w t - u t‖ ∂ν) + ∫ t, ‖u t - f t‖ ∂ν :=
      integral_add (hwI.sub huI).norm (huI.sub hfI).norm
    _ < ε := by linarith

units.lean_statement: The range of the input is imposed almost everywhere; the range of the output is pointwise on the interval.
units.lean_proof: Continuous approximation, clipping, uniform smoothing, positive shift, and integral triangle inequality.
assumptions: The endpoints \(a,b\) are real with \(a\le b\). All integrals are Lebesgue integrals restricted to the closed interval \([a,b]\). The case \(a=b\) is included.
The constants satisfy \(C\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). The function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable.
The range condition \(0\le f(t)\le C\) holds almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). No condition is placed on its values outside that interval or on its exceptional null set.
units.boundary: The approximation is for one prescribed finite interval and tolerance. Smoothness holds on all of \(\mathbb R\); positivity and the displayed upper bound are guaranteed on \([a,b]\). This result controls coefficient integrals. Convergence of solutions and passage of density estimates to limits require further arguments.

units.title: One approximation for a coefficient and its noise amplitude
units.statement: Under the same assumptions there is one globally smooth function \(g\), positive and at most \(C+\varepsilon\) on \([a,b]\), for which both the integrated coefficient error and the integrated squared error of the noise amplitude \(\sqrt{2f}\) are less than \(\varepsilon\).

steps.title: Use the coefficient theorem at half tolerance
steps.text: Choose the same \(g\) from the preceding result with tolerance \(\varepsilon/2\). Its pointwise upper bound is even \(C+\varepsilon/2\), and both coefficient functions are integrable.
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨g, hg, hgRange, hgL1⟩ :=
    exists_smooth_pos_of_ae_nonneg_bounded hab hC (half_pos hε) f hf hRange
  let ν := volume.restrict (Icc a b)
  have hν : ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, t ∈ Icc a b := ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Icc
  have hgI : Integrable g ν :=
    Integrable.of_bound hg.continuous.aestronglyMeasurable (C + ε / 2)
      (hν.mono fun t ht => by
        simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg (hgRange t ht).1.le] using (hgRange t ht).2)
  have hfI : Integrable f ν :=
    Integrable.of_bound hf.aestronglyMeasurable C
      (hRange.mono fun t ht => by simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ht.1] using ht.2)

steps.title: Compare square roots without a positive lower bound
steps.text: For nonnegative \(x,y\), split into \(x\le y\) and \(y\le x\), expand the square, and use monotonicity of square root. This proves the estimate even when either input is zero.
steps.lean:
private theorem sq_sqrt_sub_sqrt_le_abs_sub {x y : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hy : 0 ≤ y) :
    (Real.sqrt x - Real.sqrt y) ^ 2 ≤ |x - y| := by
  rcases le_total x y with h | h
  · rw [abs_of_nonpos (sub_nonpos.mpr h)]
    nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hx, Real.sq_sqrt hy,
      mul_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg x) (sub_nonneg.mpr (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h))]
  · rw [abs_of_nonneg (sub_nonneg.mpr h)]
    nlinarith [Real.sq_sqrt hx, Real.sq_sqrt hy,
      mul_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg y) (sub_nonneg.mpr (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt h))]

steps.title: Integrate the pointwise comparison
steps.text: Apply that inequality to \(x=2g(t)\), \(y=2f(t)\) almost everywhere. The squared noise error is measurable and dominated by an integrable coefficient error, so it is integrable. Integration gives the strict error bound for the same \(g\).
steps.lean:
let A (t : ℝ) := ‖Real.sqrt (2 * g t) - Real.sqrt (2 * f t)‖ ^ 2
  have hA : Measurable A :=
    ((Real.continuous_sqrt.measurable.comp (measurable_const.mul hg.continuous.measurable)).sub
      (Real.continuous_sqrt.measurable.comp (measurable_const.mul hf))).norm.pow_const 2
  have hABound : ∀ᵐ t ∂ν, A t ≤ 2 * ‖g t - f t‖ := by
    filter_upwards [hν, hRange] with t ht hft
    have hs := sq_sqrt_sub_sqrt_le_abs_sub (x := 2 * g t) (y := 2 * f t)
      (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (hgRange t ht).1.le)
      (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) hft.1)
    simpa only [A, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs, ← mul_sub, abs_mul, abs_of_nonneg (show 0 ≤ (2 : ℝ) by norm_num)] using hs
  have hDI : Integrable (fun t => 2 * ‖g t - f t‖) ν := (hgI.sub hfI).norm.const_mul 2
  have hAI : Integrable A ν := hDI.mono' hA.aestronglyMeasurable
    (hABound.mono fun t ht => by simpa [Real.norm_of_nonneg (sq_nonneg _), A] using ht)
  refine ⟨g, hg, fun t ht => ⟨(hgRange t ht).1, by linarith [(hgRange t ht).2]⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact hgL1.trans (half_lt_self hε)
  have hAInt := integral_mono_ae hAI hDI hABound
  rw [integral_const_mul] at hAInt
  change (∫ t, A t ∂ν) < ε
  linarith

units.lean_statement: A single existentially quantified smooth function satisfies both errors simultaneously.
units.lean_proof: The coefficient error at half tolerance dominates the square-integral error of the square-root noise amplitude.
assumptions: The endpoints \(a,b\) are real with \(a\le b\). All integrals are Lebesgue integrals restricted to the closed interval \([a,b]\). The case \(a=b\) is included.
The constants satisfy \(C\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\). The function \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable.
The range condition \(0\le f(t)\le C\) holds almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). No condition is placed on its values outside that interval or on its exceptional null set.

In the noise integral, Lean uses the total real square root, which is zero at negative inputs. Equivalently, replace \(f\) by a measurable nonnegative function agreeing with it almost everywhere on \([a,b]\). Its values on the exceptional null set do not affect this integral.
units.boundary: The approximation is for one prescribed finite interval and tolerance. Smoothness holds on all of \(\mathbb R\); positivity and the displayed upper bound are guaranteed on \([a,b]\). This result controls coefficient integrals. Convergence of solutions and passage of density estimates to limits require further arguments.
